criteria.name: Significance
criteria.description: Importance of the problem and of the contribution to the field.

criteria.name: Novelty
criteria.description: Technical difference from directly related prior work; absence of found prior work is not proof of first proposal.

criteria.name: Technical soundness
criteria.description: Definitions, assumptions, derivations and algorithms are consistent with the claims.

criteria.name: Evidence quality
criteria.description: Experiments, proofs or measurements actually support each core claim within its stated scope.

criteria.name: Reproducibility
criteria.description: Enough detail, code, data and settings to reproduce the main results.

criteria.name: Clarity
criteria.description: Presentation, internal consistency and correct citation.

checks.name: Claim-evidence alignment
questions: For each core claim: which specific table, figure, theorem or section supports it, and under which conditions?
Is the claim stated more broadly than the evidence (datasets, settings, model scales, populations) supports?
Are qualifiers in the original text (e.g. 'in most settings', 'on average') preserved in the abstract and conclusion?
evidence_needed: verbatim quote of the supporting or conflicting result
must_not: Do not add universal quantifiers the authors did not write.
Absence of a problem found is not proof that all properties hold.

checks.name: Method and theory soundness
questions: Are variables, domains, assumptions and constraints defined before use and used consistently?
Does the algorithm description match what the claims and experiments rely on?
For each theorem: are the conditions stated; is a proof or proof sketch provided; are there gaps?
evidence_needed: the exact step that fails or is missing
must_not: A missing proof is 'insufficient argument', not 'the theorem is false'.
A counterexample refutes a proposition only if it satisfies the proposition's own conditions.
Finite tests passing do not prove a general theorem.
Non-convexity, integer variables or an algorithm's running time alone do not prove NP-hardness.

checks.name: Experimental validity
questions: Does each research question map to an experiment that can answer it?
Are splits, baselines, hyper-parameters and resources described well enough to judge fairness?
When several factors change at once, is the gain attributed to only one of them?
evidence_needed: quotes of the setup and of the result table/caption
must_not: A missing experiment is a major issue only if it affects a specific claim.
Lack of isolation evidence does not show a component is useless or that data are fabricated.

checks.name: Novelty and positioning
checks.name_zh: 创新性与相关工作定位
questions: Which closest prior works does the paper itself cite, and how does it state its difference?
Using `sreview lit search` with public concepts only: are there directly comparable works not discussed?
Was a found work public before the submission cutoff? Is enough of its content read to judge technical equivalence?
must_not: Same model name or keyword is not technical equivalence.
Title/DOI/authors only establish identity; technical criticism needs enough full text.
Work made public after the submission cutoff is background, not a missing citation.
Never search the manuscript title or distinctive sentences for an anonymous submission.

checks.name: Internal consistency
questions: Do dataset names, sample counts, metrics, method names and table/figure numbers agree across abstract, method, results, appendix and conclusion?
Do numbers quoted in the text match the tables?
evidence_needed: both conflicting quotes with block ids
must_not: A suspected label swap needs cross-checking with sample counts and recomputable metrics; close numbers alone are not proof.

checks.name: Reproducibility information
questions: Are code, data, environment, hyper-parameters, seeds and hardware stated?
Could an expert re-run the main experiment from the paper and appendix alone?
evidence_needed: quotes of what is and is not provided
must_not: Not being able to run something is not evidence the paper is wrong.

checks.name: Citation integrity
questions: Do key citations exist and do they support the sentence they are attached to?
must_not: A missing DOI does not make a reference fake.
A preprint and its published version are one contribution.

checks.name: Presentation
questions: Are there unclear definitions, logical jumps or terminology drift that hinder understanding of the contribution?
must_not: Style preferences are minor; never list language polishing as a major concern.
